dedupe_keys.name: cdri airport resilience tool hazard specific risk reduction measures protocols and case studies for airport components

description: The Airport Resilience Tool of the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure, built with Build Change and with contributions from ACI World and the airport planners NACO, gives airport planners and operators risk reduction guidance for the hazards they face. The tool page read on 2026-09-28 lets users filter recommendations by hazard type, airport component, measure category, operational phase and time horizon, and returns suggested measures, industry protocols, assessment frameworks and real-world case studies. Hazards include cyclones, drought, dust storms, earthquake shaking, liquefaction and tsunami, fog, high wind, pluvial, tidal and storm surge flooding, heatwaves, groundwater rise, sea-level rise, snow and icing, lightning, volcanic eruptions and wildfires; components include airfields, terminal buildings, communication networks, drainage, electrical and fuel systems, and emergency management. Coverage is global. Access is free on the web; no licence is stated. Caveats: it is a guidance library, not a quantitative model, and case study sources must be checked. It supports resilience and adaptation planning of airports, such as listing drainage and power measures for a coastal airport facing storm surge. Related record: the UNDRR and CDRI country applications of infrastructure resilience.
